title: config-digger Agent definition
description: Where an Agent keeps its configuration, in which format, and with what precedence.

format_version.description: The version of this file format. Must be 1.

process.description:
How to tell that the Agent is running. Without it, config-digger
never finds it running.

homes.description: The Agent homes this Agent can have.

scopes.description:
The Scopes this Agent applies Entries at, in display order. A Scope is
only a label: precedence comes from the order of locations in `items`.

projects.description: Where this Agent records the Projects it has been started on.

locations.description: The configuration locations this Agent reads.

name.description: The display name, such as `Claude Code`.

ProcessDefinition.description:
How to tell that an Agent is running. It runs when a process matches
`images`, `paths` and `cmdline_contains`, or a session file names a PID
that is alive. Detection is best-effort: it warns or blocks a write, and
config-digger never closes an Agent.

images.description: Image names, such as `claude.exe`, compared case-insensitively.

paths.description:
Globs the executable's path must match one of, when set, such as
`~/.local/bin/claude.exe`: Claude Code and Claude Desktop are both
`claude.exe`. A glob starts with `~/`, `%NAME%` or a drive; `*` and
`?` stay within one folder name and `{a,b}` is either. Compared
case-insensitively. A process whose path the OS hides matches on its
image alone.

cmdline_contains.description:
Text the command line must contain, every one of them, compared
case-insensitively, such as Gemini CLI's script in `node.exe`.

session_files.description:
Files the Agent keeps per running session, each naming a PID that
counts only while it is alive.

SessionFiles.description: Files an Agent keeps for each running session, naming its PID.

oneOf.description:
One file per session directly in a folder, named `<pid>.<extension>`,
such as Claude Code's `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`. Only the names are
read, never the content, which can hold a Secret.

Locator.description: Where one root of an Agent home lives.

oneOf.description: A fixed path below the user's home folder, written `~/<relative path>`.

roots.description: Named roots of the home. The home is found when any root exists.

process.description:
How to tell that the Agent of this home is running, in place of the
definition's `[process]`, such as for a home whose Agent runs from
another binary.

registries.description:
Each registry adds the Projects it records. Projects found by any Agent
are evaluated for every Agent.

Registry.description: Where an Agent records the Projects it has been started on.

oneOf.description: The keys of an object in a strict JSON file, each one a Project path.

anchor.description: Where the file is. It must not lie in a Project.

root.description: The key path of the object whose keys are Project paths.

Anchor.description: What a location's path is relative to.

oneOf.description: A root of the Agent home, or a path below it.

root.description: The name of a root declared by every home of the definition.

path.description: A `/`-separated path relative to the root. Omitted when the root is the location.

oneOf.description: A path in the Project folder itself.

path.description: A `/`-separated path relative to the Project folder.

root.description:
The key path of the object whose keys are Entries. One segment may be
`{project}`: each key there is a Project path, and the Entries below it
apply only in that Project.

scope.description: The id of a declared Scope.

provenance.description: The base Provenance of the location's Entries.

store_class.description: How the location's file behaves while the Agent runs.

interpolation.description:
How the Agent writes references in this location's values. Without
it, every value is literal text.

secrets.description:
Fields of this location's Entries that hold Secrets, or that never
do, beyond what the core masks by default.

Format.description: The file format and dialect a location is read in.

oneOf.description: Strict JSON: no comments, no trailing commas.

Provenance.description: How the Entries of a location got there, which decides how they can be taken away.

oneOf.description: A key someone wrote into a configuration file, by hand or through the Agent.

StoreClass.description:
How a store config-digger writes behaves while its Agent runs, which
decides whether a write warns or is blocked then.

oneOf.description:
A file the Agent reads and leaves alone: a write while it runs warns
that it may not see the change until it restarts.

A file the Agent rewrites from memory while it runs, such as
`~/.claude.json`: a write while it runs warns strongly that the Agent
may overwrite it.

A SQLite database the Agent holds open: a write while it runs is
blocked, whatever is acknowledged.

Interpolation.description:
How an Agent writes a reference to a value it reads elsewhere, such as an
environment variable. A value made only of references is not a Secret.

oneOf.description:
`${NAME}`, where `NAME` is a letter or `_` followed by letters, digits
and `_`, plus `${namespace:argument}` for each listed namespace, and
`${NAME<separator>default}` when a default separator is set, whose
default is literal text.

SecretFields.description:
Key paths below an Entry, one key per segment, where `*` stands for any
key or array index.

fields.description:
Fields whose values are Secrets. Below an object or array, every
value is.

variable_names.description:
Fields that hold the name of a variable, such as Codex's
`bearer_token_env_var`: never a Secret, whatever else says so.

file_fields.description:
Key paths from the root of the file, outside any Entry, whose values
are Secrets, such as an API key stored next to the Entries. They are
masked wherever the file's text is shown, as in a diff's context lines.

precedence.description: Location ids of this kind, highest precedence first.

disable.description:
How the Agent Disables an Entry, in its order of preference.
Disable uses the first that covers the Entry and applies in the
context, skipping any whose target is git-versioned.

Competition.description: How same-kind Entries of one Agent home compete.

oneOf.description: Entries compete when their names are exactly equal.

DisableMechanism.description:
How an Agent Disables an Entry. An Item kind lists its mechanisms in
the Agent's order of preference.

oneOf.description:
A list of names in a JSON file: the Agent skips every Entry of an Item
whose name is in it.

locations.description:
The ids of the locations whose Entries it Disables. Omitted, it
Disables Entries of every location of the Item kind.

Target.description: The key a mechanism writes, in a file outside or inside a Project.

key_path.description:
The key path of the value written. One segment may be `{project}`:
the context's Project key, so that the switch applies only there.

store_class.description: How the target's file behaves while the Agent runs.
